rule: the train with the higher number waits; the lower number overtakes
note: GAPEKA overtakes follow it in 98 % (564; 100 % between train types, 89 % within a type)

rule: the lower number has priority: place the crossing where it keeps running (the higher number waits in the loop)
note: GAPEKA crossings follow it in 74 % (82 % between types, 67 % within a type)

rule: when the higher number cannot be held in time (the lower number reaches the crossing loop first and the other is still in the section) the train that arrives first waits
note: the exceptions in GAPEKA are of this kind: the first to arrive stops (user)

rule: equal numbers (e.g. 2501 / 2501F): the regular train before the facultative one
real GAPEKA trains keep who waits as printed (remarks x / = / //) and their printed times
note: the priority rule is only for trains the simulator plans itself

rule: a train longer than the station's Roman tracks can still be crossed: it departs first; the other train must stop and fit a track (or the two use non-adjacent tracks)
note: track lengths: infra.db station_tracks; train length: gapeka.db consists. GAPEKA: Rogojampi / Temuguruh / Singosari waits by long trains all follow it (research/layout_checks.py)

rule: every train involved in an overtake must fit the track it stands on (effective length)
trains standing at a station at the same time never exceed its Roman (main + siding) tracks; Arabic-numbered tracks are stabling / yard only
note: GAPEKA: 296 stations checked, no exceedance except two diagrams read only in part (research/layout_checks.py)
